canon-eos-m200: Compact and fun for the money; many miss a viewfinder, a proper grip and customisable buttons.
canon-eos-m50: Small, light and easy first camera with good value and image quality; short battery, few buttons.
canon-eos-r10: Light, compact body with a good grip and real controls, but no stabilisation or weather sealing.
canon-eos-r100: Great-value light entry camera for a first or travel body, though autofocus struggles with birds.
canon-eos-r5-mark-ii: Pre-capture and high resolution for cropping sports and wildlife; video heat is a common gripe.
canon-eos-r50: Small, light and good value for a first camera; several report mode dial or shutter failures.
canon-eos-r50-v: Small video-first body with C-Log3 that also shoots good stills; no viewfinder is the gripe.
canon-eos-r6-mark-ii: Sticky autofocus and good battery for long shoots, though some find the colours dull or greenish.
canon-eos-r6-mark-iii: Pre-capture and resolution for cropping, though several find high-ISO noise slightly worse.
canon-eos-r7: Crop reach and a comfortable grip for wildlife and sport; the main gripe is inconsistent autofocus.
canon-eos-r8: Full-frame quality in a very light body at a fair price; the grip rubber wears or peels for some.
canon-powershot-v1: Pocketable video camera with a wide 16mm end and built-in ND, but battery life is short.
dji-osmo-action-6: Clean low light and smooth stabilisation in a compact body; a few report short-lived shutdowns and glitches.
dji-osmo-pocket-3: Pocketable with smooth stabilisation for vlogs and travel; delicate and not water resistant.
dji-osmo-pocket-4: Pocketable gimbal with sharp video and smooth stabilisation; a few find it fragile or the app a chore.
fujifilm-gfx100-ii: Medium-format stills with snappy autofocus and good handling; heavy, and not ideal for fast action.
fujifilm-gfx100rf: Medium-format files in a compact fixed-lens body; the f/4 lens and no IBIS limit low light for some.
fujifilm-gfx100s: Studio-grade files and strong dynamic range in a handy medium-format body; heavy, a few failures.
fujifilm-x-e5: Small, premium-feeling body with interchangeable lenses; weak battery life and a touchy eye sensor.
fujifilm-x-half: Tiny, fun, film-like pocket camera, but many find it overpriced for fair image quality.
fujifilm-x-m5: Tiny and light for everyday carry, though the missing viewfinder is hard to live with in bright sun.
fujifilm-x-s20: Deep grip and long battery in a small body; overheating in video is the top complaint.
fujifilm-x-t5: Tactile dials and lighter than most full frame; autofocus trails rivals on moving subjects.
fujifilm-x100vi: Colours and film simulations that people carry everywhere; autofocus is slow for kids and low light.
gopro-mission-1: Cleaner low light and dynamic range than earlier models; a couple find it heavy and harder to grade.
hasselblad-907x-cfv-100c: Lovely colour and a tactile, well-built body that is a joy to shoot; autofocus struggles and it is pricey.
hasselblad-x2d-100c: Rich, true-to-life colour from huge files, with stabilisation that holds at slow shutter speeds; pricey.
hasselblad-x2d-ii-100c: Excellent stills with very effective stabilisation and much better continuous autofocus; a steep price.
insta360-luna-ultra: Strong low light and a handy detachable screen; overheating shuts it down in long 4K clips.
insta360-x5: Strong low-light 360 video with replaceable lenses; bulky, with slow, laborious editing.
leica-d-lux-8: Pocketable with a sharp zoom and a good viewfinder; the high price for an older sensor stings.
leica-q3: Sharp lens and simple menus make it a favourite travel camera, though autofocus lags on moving kids.
leica-q3-43: Exceptionally sharp APO lens and simple handling; autofocus is slow for Sony or Canon converts.
leica-q3-monochrom: Clean high-ISO files and tonal black and white with strong low light.
leica-sl3-p: Fine skin tones, a sturdy sealed body and video options; some find autofocus behind rivals and the price high.
nikon-coolpix-p1100: Huge zoom with steady stabilisation reaches what nothing else can; heavy, with weak software.
nikon-z30: Small, light travel and vlogging camera, though the missing viewfinder bothers some.
nikon-z50: Comfortable grip and sharp kit lens make a good first or travel camera; weaker in low light than older bodies.
nikon-z50ii: Subject-detect autofocus that copes with birds and action for the price; no stabilisation.
nikon-z5ii: Close to pricier bodies for value, with fast autofocus; a few report missed focus on moving pets.
nikon-z5iic: Full-frame stills in a light, pocketable body with a chunky grip; the missing viewfinder splits opinion.
nikon-z7: Detailed files, a very good viewfinder and comfortable handling; the lens adapter is bulky.
nikon-z8: Blackout-free viewfinder and tracking autofocus for birds; big and heavy, short battery for some.
nikon-zf: Retro, dial-driven and fun to shoot; the shallow grip is awkward with larger lenses.
om-system-om-1-mark-ii: Stabilisation that makes handheld long exposures work, plus quick autofocus; low-light wildlife is a limit.
om-system-om-5-mark-ii: Small, sealed body with strong stabilisation and a deep grip at a fair price; a few report focus problems.
om-system-om-d-e-m10-mark-iv: Tiny, light body with in-body stabilisation at a low price; a few report lens and screen failures.
om-system-tough-tg-7: Waterproof, shockproof body that goes anywhere, with great macro; image quality trails larger sensors.
panasonic-lumix-g9ii: Phase-detect autofocus and stabilisation suit action and telephoto work; handheld low light is noisy.
panasonic-lumix-gh5ii: Video workhorse with excellent stabilisation, 10-bit 4K and no overheating; big and its autofocus lags.
panasonic-lumix-gh7: Phase-detect autofocus finally fixes the old complaint, with ProRes RAW and top stabilisation; chunky.
panasonic-lumix-lx10: Pocketable with real dials and files that beat a phone for some; quality and reliability are mixed.
panasonic-lumix-s1h: Cinema-grade video with a cooling fan, great screen and excellent battery; very big and heavy.
panasonic-lumix-s1ii: Very fast bursts, a robust layout and 6K video with stabilisation; costly, and the buffer needs watching.
panasonic-lumix-s1rii: High-resolution stills with fast bursts at a lower price; video has some readout and autofocus caveats.
panasonic-lumix-s5iix: Video-first hybrid with ProRes, SSD recording and great stabilisation; some feel stills are an afterthought.
panasonic-lumix-zs99: Pocket body with a 30x zoom that reaches subjects phones cannot; small sensor struggles in low light.
ricoh-gr-iiix: Truly pocketable with sharp images that many carry everywhere; autofocus is weak.
ricoh-gr-iv: Pocketable with a great lens, often shot more than bigger cameras; fixed 28mm takes adjusting to.
ricoh-gr-iv-monochrome: Pocketable black-and-white with sharp lens, clean high ISO and stabilisation; steep price for a niche.
sigma-bf: Machined aluminium body with clean menus and rich colour that invites shooting; awkward to hold for some.
sony-a6700: Superb tracking autofocus in a compact body with plenty of lenses; overheats in long 4K video.
sony-a7-ii: Full-frame quality and stabilisation at a low used price; poor menus and battery life frustrate many.
sony-a7-v: AI autofocus and pre-capture for sports and birds; some upgraders see little image difference.
sony-a7c-ii: One of the smallest full-frame bodies with near automatic autofocus; front-heavy with big lenses.
sony-a9-iii: Blistering autofocus and handling for sports; several complain about noise at high ISO and the price.
sony-rx10-v: One lens covers 24-600mm with fast bursts and a sharp viewfinder; autofocus can miss and it is pricey.
sony-rx100-iv: Pocketable with sharp 1-inch files and 4K video; menus feel fiddly and some prefer a phone.
sony-rx100-vii: Long zoom and pop-up viewfinder in a pocket, though a few find it fragile or slow to operate.
sony-rx1r-iii: Full-frame sharpness in a pocket body, great for travel and street; battery life and price are the gripes.
sony-zv-1: Pocketable with strong video features and autofocus for vlogging; some find stills and menus underwhelming.
sony-zv-1-ii: Pocket vlogging camera with strong autofocus and a wide zoom; no optical stabilisation, and it can overheat.
sony-zv-1f: Light, easy beginner vlogger with a wide lens and simple menus; autofocus and still quality disappoint some.
sony-zv-e1: Clean low-light video in a small full-frame body with strong stabilisation; some report overheating.
sony-zv-e10-ii: Affordable interchangeable-lens vlogging with good 4K and a better battery; overheats in 60p for several.
